newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up, hedging trims gains late.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up, hedging trims gains late.

text.p: WCE canola ended with sharp gains Monday, rallying in line with gains in the CBOT soy complex, floor traders said.
"We followed Chicago and closed higher, but hedge pressure on the close knocked us off our highs," said a WCE floor trader.
CBOT soybean futures rallied on ideas that an impending port strike in Brazil will significantly slow the pace of soy exports from that country, traders said.
Both feed wheat and barley futures ended lower on increased commercial selling in late trade, traders said.
"The commercials increased their selling ideas to reflect increased country movement of wheat over the weekend," one floor trader said.
Canola ended up $1.80 to $4.90 with March up $4.00 at $413.70 a tonne. March flax closed up $2.00 at $353.00.
Barley settled down $2.50 to $0.30, with March down $0.40 at $140.80. Feed wheat settled down $1.50 to $2.60, with March down $1.60 at $173.60.
December feed peas ended down US$0.50 at US$189.00. Oats closed up slightly with May up US$1.70 at US$127.50 in line with the CBOT.
(Values in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats and peas.)
